system_description.narrative_title: Iran de‑escalation signals reshape oil markets amid Houthi attacks
system_description.narrative_summary: A single dominant narrative ties US restraint and diplomatic overtures over the Iran conflict to falling oil prices, even as continuing Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and regional military movements keep geopolitical risk elevated. The system is open: political signals (US statements, diplomacy) interact with military actions (strikes, interceptions), energy flows (pipeline and exports), and market responses (oil/gas prices), producing feedbacks that influence further policy and market behaviour.
system_description.scope: Actors, processes and assets directly involved in the Iran‑related conflict and its economic effects: US administration statements and diplomacy (Trump, advisers), Iran and Iranian proxies (Houthis), Gulf states (Saudi, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait), Iraq (border/export arrangements), energy infrastructure (pipelines, Aramco facilities, Hormuz transit), global oil and fuel markets, and public/political reactions in the US and region.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical‑economic system centered on energy security, international conflict dynamics, and commodity markets
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil and commodities markets and trading infrastructure
U.S. domestic politics and electoral accountability
Gulf security architecture and regional military coalitions
Proxy warfare and non‑state actor operations in Yemen
evidence_headlines: Trump says renewed Iran strikes ‘highly unlikely’ if talks progress but warns he could still strike
Oil prices hit 10-week low after Donald Trump says strikes on Iran ‘highly unlikely’
Saudi Arabia’s vital East-West pipeline struck in attack
Saudi Aramco office in Riyadh damaged in latest Houthi strikes
Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar, no imminent deal seen to end the war
Iran defends two-day proposal for peace talks after US rejects conditions

variables.name: Diplomatic signal tone
variables.description: The aggregate adversarial-versus-conciliatory tone of official diplomatic communications and public statements about the conflict.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The frequency and scale of formal diplomatic contacts, negotiations and mediations per unit time.

variables.name: Military action intensity
variables.description: The overall level of kinetic military operations, strikes and force deployments in the region.

variables.name: Proxy attack frequency
variables.description: The rate at which indirect or proxy attacks (for example missile and drone launches) are initiated per unit time.

variables.name: Air defense interception rate
variables.description: The rate at which defensive systems successfully detect and intercept incoming aerial threats.

variables.name: Energy infrastructure damage rate
variables.description: The rate at which energy production, refining or transport assets sustain physical damage.

variables.name: Energy export throughput
variables.description: The volume of crude oil and refined fuels exported through regional routes per unit time.

variables.name: Oil supply disruption level
variables.description: The aggregate reduction in available oil supply relative to baseline due to operational constraints, blockages and outages.

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: A benchmark crude price index representing the prevailing international oil price level.

variables.name: Market risk premium
variables.description: The additional price component on energy commodities reflecting investor assessments of geopolitical and supply risk.

variables.name: Oil inventory stock
variables.description: The aggregate commercial oil stocks held in storage regionally and globally.

variables.name: Fuel retail price level
variables.description: The average consumer pump price level for refined transport fuels.

variables.name: Shipping transit risk
variables.description: The perceived hazard and disruption probability for maritime energy transport corridors.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: Short-term variance or volatility in energy commodity prices and futures markets.

variables.name: Public support for military action
variables.description: The level of public approval for initiating, expanding or continuing military operations related to the conflict.

variables.name: Economic demand for oil
variables.description: Aggregate commercial and consumer demand for crude oil and petroleum products across markets.

catalysts.title: Trump meeting with Qatar mediator
catalysts.description: A high‑level meeting between President Trump and Qatar’s prime minister/mediator to discuss Iran could occur, shaping U.S. public posture and diplomatic momentum.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Trump to meet Qatar's prime minister', 'Trump downplays prospect of new Iran strikes', 'Trump to meet Iran war mediator Qatar'.

catalysts.title: Restart of US‑Iran peace talks
catalysts.description: Diplomatic negotiations or structured talks (including outreach by envoys) to de‑escalate the conflict could resume, altering risk perceptions and attacks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Vance reaches out to Iranian hard‑liner', 'Iran defends two‑day proposal', 'Trump signals restraint'.

catalysts.title: Continued Houthi attacks on Gulf targets
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi missile/drone and sabotage strikes against Saudi and regional energy infrastructure are likely to persist, keeping physical risks elevated.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi East‑West pipeline struck', 'Houthi attack damages Aramco building', 'Iconic Saudi Tower Hit'.

catalysts.title: Gulf military command implementation
catalysts.description: Activation and operationalization of the approved Gulf Arab military command HQ in Kuwait will increase coordinated defense and interception capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Gulf Arab states approve military command headquarters in Kuwait' signalling coordinated defenses.

catalysts.title: Iraq limits Iran border crossings
catalysts.description: Iraq’s implementation of U.S. requests to shut most Iran border crossings and arrangements on exports through Hormuz may constrain Iranian logistics while easing export routes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US asks Iraq to shut most Iran border crossings', 'Iraq reached understandings to allow oil exports through Hormuz'.

catalysts.title: Thanksgiving travel fuel demand spike
catalysts.description: U.S. Thanksgiving travel surge (Nov 26) will raise short‑term fuel demand and retail pump prices, tightening inventories temporarily.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Thanksgiving fuel costs will still be the highest since 2000' and falling U.S. gas prices noted.

catalysts.title: Risk of limited U.S. strikes if talks collapse
catalysts.description: If diplomatic efforts fail, the U.S. could order targeted strikes on Iranian or proxy assets, abruptly raising military and market risks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'U.S. Warns Gulf of Possible Short, Intense Renewal', 'Trump’s clashing advisers press him to make Iran war decision', but he signals restraint.
